rv.q: A mighty, moving and sometimes messy piece of theatre, it's really, at heart, a state-of-the-nation play.
Sheen burns with genuine passion. His charisma fills the gaps in the script.
Michael Sheen brings zest to this lumpy story of the founder of the NHS
Sheen catches Nye's lightning in a bottle.
Nye's story deserves to echo through the ages.
It's a stirring performance in a drama that has a tendency to romanticise the NHS without offering or inspiring a sufficient rallying cry to save it.

cn.t: Michael Sheen's passionate performance elevates this uneven biographical drama about NHS founder Aneurin Bevan. Critics praise its ambition as a state-of-the-nation piece but find the storytelling lumpy and overly romanticized.
